RequiredOrItems.description: Object keywords constrain only the objects and array keywords only the arrays.

ContainsOrClosed.description: So do contains and unevaluatedProperties, which contains does not evaluate for.

ContainsOrPrefixed.description: String keywords beside them constrain the strings, which are a kind the value can be.

RequiredOrEmpty.description: So do string lengths beside object keywords.

ItemsOrNumber.description: Bounds constrain the numbers, of which they admit more than TypeScript can list.

RequiredOrMemberItems.description: allOf members without type ask the same value, so their keywords count with the schema's own.

ItemsOrMemberDependent.description: So do those of members of members.

OneOfKind.description: anyOf and oneOf members do not: each is the kinds its own keywords say.

MemberDependentOrItems.description: A member with keywords of several kinds constrains each kind by its own.

MemberKeysOrContains.description: So does one with propertyNames and contains.

MemberOrNull.description: Other kinds the parent's type names pass it.

NestedMemberOrNull.description: So does one whose own member has keywords of another kind.

EitherMemberOrNull.description: So does one whose anyOf members are of several kinds.

MemberOfAnyType.description: Without type in the parent, the member is the kinds its keywords say.

ClosedMember.description: A closed object admits no object that requires a key it forbids; the member's arrays stay.

AnyMember.description: anyOf members constrain each kind by their own keywords too.

ThenSeveralKinds.description: So does then: if admits every array, so then's maxItems applies to them.
